notes: POC context: Oreon runs per-call recommendation + reranking for edge telecom sessions (live voice -> short text -> recommend inline).
Primary constraints: extremely latency-sensitive (interactive call lateral decisions) and strict per-call unit economics.
Perf targets quoted by customer: p95 end-to-end generation < 50ms (in-path), sustained 500 qps for short prompts (avg 80 tokens), burst to 2k qps tolerated with graceful degradation.
Cost target: blended cost <= $0.002 per request at scale (model+inference infra). Customer says: "We need predictable ops costs; surprises kill the deal."

Technical asks: dynamic batching (max batch 16, target median 6), prefix / KV caching for repeated conversational templates, 4-bit/8-bit quantization profile evaluation for 2-3 candidate open models, and throughput-latency tradeoff dashboard.
Quality bar: business-critical reranker must not regress >1.5% MRR on precision@10; want automated eval hooks tied to rollouts.

Benchmark ask to Redwood: run identical benchmarking harness against Dedicated with and without quantization; provide per-token cost breakdown, kernel-level latency, and model fallback behavior under capacity pressure.
Security: must run in customer VPC/on-prem for production due to data residency and regulatory constraints; SSO/SAML + KMS integration required; retention policy 30 days then purge.

Early POC findings: batching reduced token compute by ~22% but introduced p95 tail on sporadic bursts; caching reduced repeated prefix cost by ~30% for identical templates; 4-bit quantization gave 2.8x perf uplift but requires careful eval — some hallucination spikes in reranker tests.
Sales notes: procurement expects final pricing by 2026-04; legal is pushing contract language for GPU reservation SLAs and termination rights.
Quote from ML lead (call 2026-02-27): "If Redwood can show a stable p95 under burst with a quantized model and clear cost math, we can move to annual commitment."
